exposure: Familial Mediterranean Fever (FMF) diagnosis status (before vs. after diagnosis)
FMF diagnosis status (FMF patients vs. healthy controls)
cohort: The study included 215 pregnancies from 81 women with Familial Mediterranean Fever (FMF) and 94 pregnancies from 42 healthy control women, comparing outcomes before and after FMF diagnosis as well as with controls.
finding: Maternal and neonatal outcomes in FMF pregnancies were comparable to those in controls, while advanced maternal age and disease activity before conception were identified as independent predictors of adverse maternal outcomes.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was significantly more frequent in pregnancies after FMF diagnosis compared to before diagnosis.
cross-section timing: Data was collected retrospectively, comparing obstetric and neonatal outcomes in pregnancies occurring before and after FMF diagnosis.
